3. Due Diligence and Buyer's Right to Terminate

Due diligence period - inspection_period_days  calendar days after the Binding Agreement Date

During the Due Diligence Period, Buyer and Buyer's contractors, inspectors, lenders, partners, agents, and prospective assignees may enter the Property at reasonable times after reasonable notice to inspect, photograph, measure, estimate repairs, evaluate title and zoning, and determine whether the Property meets Buyer's investment requirements. Buyer will not conduct destructive testing without Seller's written consent and will repair material physical damage directly caused by an inspection.

Buyer may terminate this Agreement for any reason or no reason by delivering written notice to Seller before the Due Diligence Period expires. Upon timely termination, earnest money will be returned to Buyer and neither party will have further obligations except obligations that expressly survive termination.

4. Property Condition and Access

Except for Seller's express representations in this Agreement, Buyer accepts the Property "AS IS, WHERE IS, WITH ALL FAULTS." Seller will maintain the Property in substantially its present condition through Closing, keep utilities on when reasonably available, and provide reasonable access. Seller will disclose known material latent defects, environmental hazards, code violations, unpermitted work, casualty damage, and pending governmental notices not readily observable by Buyer.

Seller authorizes Buyer to share Property information and privately show the Property to contractors, lenders, partners, and prospective assignees for evaluating Buyer's contractual interest. Buyer may not represent that Buyer owns the Property before Closing.

5. Title, Closing, and Possession

Seller will convey good and marketable fee-simple title by limited warranty deed or other deed acceptable to the Closing Attorney, free of monetary liens and encumbrances other than permitted exceptions accepted by Buyer. Seller will cooperate with reasonable title-curative requirements. Buyer may terminate and receive a return of earnest money if material title defects are not cured by Closing, or Buyer may waive the defects in writing.

Real estate taxes, rents, association charges, utilities, and similar items will be prorated as of Closing using the Closing Attorney's customary method. Seller will pay liens, delinquent taxes, deed preparation, and Seller's obligations. Buyer will pay Buyer's recording, title, financing, and due-diligence costs. Other costs will be allocated by the Closing Attorney's customary practice unless stated below.

Special closing-cost allocation, if any 

Seller will deliver vacant possession at Closing unless otherwise stated. Keys, access devices, leases, security deposits, and transferable service records will be delivered at Closing.

Occupancy or possession exception, if any

6. Seller Representations

Seller represents to Buyer, through Closing, that:

  1. Seller has authority to enter this Agreement and convey the Property.
  2. No other binding sale, option, right of first refusal, or undisclosed lease prevents this sale.
  3. Seller has disclosed all titled owners and persons whose signatures are required.
  4. Seller is not relying on Buyer for legal, tax, appraisal, probate, bankruptcy, or financial advice.
  5. Seller has not received notice of pending condemnation or governmental taking except as disclosed below.
  6. Information Seller provides about occupancy, leases, liens, utilities, condition, and authority is materially accurate to Seller's knowledge.
Exceptions to Seller representations 

7. Principal Buyer; No Brokerage Relationship

Buyer is acting solely as a principal for Buyer's own investment account and is not acting as Seller's real-estate broker, agent, fiduciary, appraiser, or advisor. Buyer may renovate, rent, resell, finance, or assign Buyer's contractual interest for a profit. Seller understands that Buyer's profit may be substantial and that the Purchase Price may differ from appraised value, assessed value, or a price obtainable through a traditional listed sale. Seller may obtain independent valuation, brokerage, legal, tax, and financial advice before signing.

If required because an unsolicited monetary offer is below the prior year's county assessed value, include the following additional notice before delivery:
THIS OFFER IS LESS THAN THE COUNTY ASSESSED VALUE FOR THIS PROPERTY.

8. Assignment

Buyer may assign this Agreement and Buyer's rights and obligations, in whole or in part, to an affiliated entity, funding partner, or third-party purchaser without further consent from Seller. Seller consents to such assignment. Buyer will provide notice of assignment to Seller or the Closing Attorney. Unless Seller separately releases Buyer in writing, an assignment does not release Buyer from obligations that remain enforceable under this Agreement.

9. Casualty and Condemnation

Risk of loss remains with Seller until Closing. If material casualty damage or condemnation occurs before Closing, Buyer may terminate and receive a return of earnest money or proceed and receive any assignable insurance or condemnation proceeds and credits available to Seller.

10. Default and Remedies

If Buyer defaults after the Due Diligence Period without a contractual right to terminate, Seller's sole monetary remedy will be retention of earnest money as liquidated damages, except for obligations that expressly survive. If Seller defaults, Buyer may terminate and receive earnest money plus documented third-party inspection and title costs, or pursue any remedy available under Georgia law. The parties acknowledge that remedies can depend on the facts and applicable law.

11. Federal and Property-Specific Disclosures

For residential improvements built before 1978, the parties must complete the federally required lead-based-paint disclosure and Seller must provide the required EPA pamphlet before Buyer is obligated, unless a lawful exemption applies. Seller will provide any other disclosure required for the Property, including applicable community-association, flood, septic, well, tenant, or local disclosures.

13. General Terms

Time is of the essence. This Agreement and its signed exhibits are the entire agreement and replace prior discussions concerning the Property. Amendments, waivers, and terminations must be in writing and signed by the affected parties. Invalid provisions will be severed without invalidating the remainder. No waiver is continuing. This Agreement binds and benefits the parties and permitted successors and assigns. Georgia law governs. Electronic signatures, counterparts, and electronically delivered copies will be treated as originals.
